meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/01, Thursday 15 May 2025). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: First OCR paper. OCR breaks both other boards' conventions: every J560 paper is 100 marks (not 80), and it is papers 2 and 5 that are non-calculator, not paper 1. Marks per part are printed as [N] in the right margin of the QP; OCR prints no per-question total, so every part total was read individually and the paper checked against the printed 100.

coding_notes: OCR prints NO 'Total for Question N' line — only a bare [N] against each part. The only available check is the whole-paper sum against the printed 100, which this file passes.

OCR overlaps its tiers like Edexcel, but INTERLEAVED rather than as one contiguous block: q18, q19, q21, q23, q25 and q29 of this paper reappear as q1, q2, q4, q5, q8 and q9 of J560/04 (Higher). Those items carry identical marks and identical tags in both files.

q3 (reflect a trapezium in a mirror line) tagged reflections even though that node credits eight skills including Understanding Straight Line Graphs. Unlike the Edexcel kite case, this genuinely IS a reflection, so the exact node is right and the over-credit is a property of data/skills.ts rather than of the tagging.

q6a/q6b (scale drawing: measure a distance, then plot a point at a bearing) tagged with measuring_lines_and_angles as the second skill — the doc warns that node is about protractor use, which here is exactly what the question demands.
q18 tagged exact_calculations: its example in data/skills.ts is literally 'use your calculator to work out ...', which is what this question is.
q22 (simple interest, find the rate) tagged percentage_change, NOT growth_and_decay — growth_and_decay is compound, and simple interest demonstrates nothing about a repeated multiplier.

q23a (decide whether each statement is an equation or an identity) tagged expanding_double_brackets: the taxonomy has no equation-vs-identity node, and expanding the brackets is the only way to tell them apart.
q15 (match sketched graphs to equations) tagged sketching_functions rather than quadratic_functions — the demand is recognising standard graph shapes, and sketching_functions credits fewer skills.
